newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Belgrade bourse turnover halved in week to Dec 6.
newsitem.headline: Belgrade bourse turnover halved in week to Dec 6.

text.p: The Belgrade Stock Exchange (BSE) reported on Monday a 50.58 percent decline in its turnover during the week ending December 6 and traders attributed the plunge to persistent lack of liquidity.
Total weekly turnover fell to 25.417 million dinars ($5.01 million) from 51.431 million dinars a week ago. The number of transactions inched higher to 184 from 172, the bourse said.

"Strong cyclical oscillations in the bourse activity are usual for short-term securities. Liquidity falls three or four times a month when tax and salaries payments are due or when banks set aside the 15 percent reserve requirement," a trader told Reuters.
Traders said the lack of trading in the central bank short-term bonds was one of the key reasons behind the sharp plunge in the BSE turnover.

"The market is very quiet and weak. This is only the beginning of a bad period ahead of the year-end book closures. There will be no market stability for the rest of the year, maybe longer," another trader said.
"But a gradual slide in the dinar black market rate worries us the most," the trader said.
The dinar black market rate slid to 3.7 from 3.4 to the German mark before the elections amid three weeks of opposition and student protests accusing the ruling Socialists of election fraud.

Belgrade and several major Serbian cities have been shaken by street demonstrations after the Socialists annulled a victory by the opposition in 15 cities, including the capital, in local elections last month.

"The slide in the dinar rate only reflects the current political situation. As long as people are out in the streets, and we do not know how the mass protest will end, the situation signals instability," one analyst said.
For the week ending December 6, the BSE reported the following details:
* Commercial paper traded 147 times for a volume of 21.198 million dinars, accounting for 83 percent of the weekly total.
* Treasury bills accounted for 3.262 million dinars in 33 transactions, or 13 percent of the total turnover.
Interest rates on commercial paper and treasury bills ranged between an annual 155.72 and 793 percent.
* The central bank auctioned on Friday a new 30 million dinar tranche of 30-day bonds, cutting the interest rate to an annual 77.9 percent from 128.29 percent.
It sold only 0.35 million dinars of bonds and withdrew nearly 15 million unsold from the previous tranche.

"There is no investor interest for those bonds because majority of commercial banks are experiencing liquidity crisis. How can you sell bonds when banks have to set aside 15 percent of their total deposits for the reserve requirement," a central bank senior official who asked not to be named said. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
